This chapter is the map of snapy for a reader who has never opened it. It follows one time step from the caller's
loop, through a `MeshBlock` or a `Mesh`, into the hydro and scalar kernels, and back out to the written outputs. It
then says where the data lives in memory, how a run is configured, how Python reaches the same objects, and which
external packages the code leans on. Every section is a code map read at the pin of `code_pin.yml`. It names the
function that does each thing and the test that holds the claim up.

One step at the pin, in brief. The caller's loop asks for $\Delta t$[^rg-473f42b9b5af] and calls `forward` once per Runge–Kutta stage on
a `MeshBlock` or a `Mesh` (@sec-ch01-driver). Each stage is a schedule of named ops built by the block's stage
executor: the stage-entry exchange of a bare block, the hydro and scalar increments, the user forcings, the
integrator's combine, and the end-of-stage slots for saturation, chemistry and the physical ghosts (@sec-ch01-stage).
The executor runs the schedule eagerly, or groups the ops into segments and replays the capturable ones as CUDA[^rg-28386113293d] graphs
(the segments, the capture and the refusal list: @sec-ch11-segments, @sec-ch11-capture, @sec-ch11-refusals; the Mesh's cuts
and agreement: @sec-ch13-cuts, @sec-ch13-agree; the capture sweep: @sec-ch16-capture). Every face flux goes through the block's flux register, which keeps the stage's totals and the step's
sums (@sec-ch01-stage). A `Mesh` runs the stages of its blocks through one executor, then its global phase, then the
exchange between its blocks (@sec-ch01-mesh, @sec-ch13). It makes no new numerical claim of its own. The
physics of each operator belongs to its own chapter, which the map points at. The directories and modules of the repository, with the chapter
that covers each, are listed in @sec-appj.

The dependency figure below is a call-ownership map: an arrow says who calls what, not that one numerical
switch implies another. The switch couplings are in @sec-ch12-matrix.

each section states the result and its run, and @sec-ch16-ch01 records their device and rank coverage. The chapter's
own checks are ports that import no snapy.
